name: Argus v4 hooked line
description: ABIs and addresses for reading Argus launches on Arc. Generated from compiled artifacts by contracts-ark/tools/abi-bundle.mjs; every address is re-read from the Portal by its --verify pass.

chain.name: Arc mainnet
notes: USDC is the gas token AND the default quote asset. The native 18dp balance and the 0x3600 ERC-20 view at 6dp are one balance, exactly 1e12 apart.
JSON-RPC batching is refused (-32600). viem batches by default; pass {batch: false}.
eth_getLogs caps at 10,000 blocks per request and 20,000 results per response, refusing the whole query either way.
Arc mines ~170,000 blocks a day. Every log carries blockTimestamp, so no per-block fetch is needed.
Native USDC transfers emit Transfer from the EIP-7708 pseudo-address 0xffff...fffe, not from 0x3600. Indexing only 0x3600 misses roughly 60% of movements.

portals.note: Every new launch goes here. The eleventh word of launches(token), index 10, is the quote asset that launch trades against, chosen per launch from the quotes the admin has approved (every launch so far uses 0x3600 USDC). launch() is not payable: the dev buy is pulled as an ERC-20 after an approve. The admin, a 2-of-3 Safe, approves and revokes quotes INSTANTLY and changes hookStore, splitterImpl and lockerImpl behind a four hour timelock, all for FUTURE launches only. tokenImpl, treasury, treasuryBps and devBuyMaxBps are immutable. Its reward registry is a new LaunchConfig, addresses.launchConfig.

Superseded by Portal #6. Its tokens keep pointing at it forever. Ten words, every launch against 0x3600 USDC, and launch() is payable: the dev buy is msg.value. The same admin and timelocked pointers as #6, without the quote list. Its reward registry is 0x71555a0674529a2bf7288193047aa1e06d267157, not addresses.launchConfig. Creator payouts are credited and delivered by claim(address) as on #6, but as a NATIVE USDC send, which Arc logs from the EIP-7708 pseudo-address rather than from 0x3600.
Superseded by Portal #5. No privileged role. The same ten-word record as #5.
LAUNCH_STRUCT_WORDS() reverts. Same struct without tickBond; confirmed 288 bytes on chain.
LAUNCH_STRUCT_WORDS() reverts. TEN words of DIFFERENT types in a different order, decoding.launchesLegacyV3. Word count alone will not tell this apart from a hooked ten-word Portal.
The first Portal. Launched ARGUS at 0xece5ca8bf9220718e5727754026757512212cb3c, which is a TOKEN and not a Portal.

discriminator.answers10OnNote: Kept a single address for v1 readers. answers10OnAll lists every Portal that answers 10.
discriminator.onOlderPortals: Reverts. Depending on the endpoint a missing selector comes back as an execution-reverted error or as 0x with trace[0].error == 'Reverted'. Treat either as 'no usable answer' and pick the decoder from the Portal address.

decoding.quoteWord: On Portal #6 a launch's quote asset is index 10, the eleventh and last word of its record, not a constant. Build the pool key, the price and the decimals from it. Every launch on a ten- or nine-word Portal is against 0x3600 USDC.
decoding.bondedIsNotInTheStruct: bonded() lives on the HOOK, which is word 4. Also bondTick() and bondBound(). The hook latches the flag inside afterSwap, in the same transaction as the swap that crosses tickBond. There is no bond() and no bondable() anywhere on this line.
decoding.poolId: keccak256(abi.encode(currency0, currency1, fee, tickSpacing, hooks)), the currencies being the token and THAT LAUNCH'S quote (index 10 on #6, 0x3600 before it) in address order. THE HOOK IS PART OF THE KEY; omitting it yields a different, empty pool id. Every Argus v4 launch uses fee 10000 and tickSpacing 200. Prefer reading it from TokenCreated.poolId or hook.poolId() over rebuilding the key.

swapLogs.emitter: Swap is emitted by the PoolManager singleton, so the pool id in topic 1 is the only thing separating your token's trades from every other v4 trade on Arc. Filtering by address alone returns the whole chain. The data is SIX words: v3's five plus a trailing uint24 fee. Amounts are int128 but sign-extended across the full word, so a v3 decoder reads them correctly after truncating to five words.
swapLogs.signConvention: 🔴 v4 SIGNS ITS AMOUNTS FROM THE SWAPPER'S SIDE, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF UNISWAP v3. On v3 a negative leg is the amount that LEFT the pool. On v4 a negative leg is what the SWAPPER PAID. So a buy of the token is `tokenAmount < 0` on v3 and `tokenAmount > 0` on v4, and a decoder shared between the two labels every trade backwards on one of them. Nothing throws and nothing looks wrong: the magnitudes are identical either way and only the side flips.
swapLogs.signConventionEvidence: Measured on Arc mainnet, not read off a doc. sqrtPriceX96 is emitted INSIDE the swap log, so the direction the pool moved is knowable from the logs alone with no opinion about which token is which, and liquidity changes do not move it. Correlating sign(amount0) against that direction across consecutive swaps in one pool: v4, 48 pairs over 13 pools, 48 swapper / 0 pool. v3, 217 pairs over 67 pools, 0 swapper / 217 pool. Unanimous both ways.
swapLogs.sideRule: isBuy = tokenLeg > 0 on v4. Take magnitudes with abs() for size and volume: those are identical under either convention, which is why a volume figure can look perfectly correct while every side is inverted.
swapLogs.quoteLegUnits: The quote leg is in that launch's quote's own decimals, 6 for USDC. Read decimals() off the quote at index 10 rather than assuming 6.

legacyTokenCreated.note: The legacy line's TokenCreated is a DIFFERENT event with a different body: its fifth field is `address pool`, not `bytes32 poolId`. Decoding a legacy log against the hooked parameter list does not throw; it returns whichever strings happen to line up. Match on topic0. Every hooked Portal, #6 included, emits the SAME hooked event: #6 declares the same nine inputs as #5, and this topic0 is present in both runtimes.

decoding.allocationIsSharesOfTheStream: creatorBps / burnBps / dividendBps / liquidityBps are proportions OF THE COLLECTED STREAM, not of a trade. A launch at creatorBps 10000 with a 1% tax sends the creator all of that 1%, which is 'Creator 100%' and not 'Creator 1%'. Multiplying the shares back out by the tax rate produces numbers that look like small independent fees.

quote.approvedNote: Quotes this bundle vouches for, each confirmed by quoteApproved(address) when this was generated. The live set can hold more: Rebuild the live set from QuoteApproved and QuoteRevoked logs on the Portal from its deploy block: the constructor emitted QuoteApproved for the default, so the logs alone are complete.
quote.admission: A launch naming a quote that is not approved reverts QuoteNotApproved, whoever calls.
quote.approve: approveQuote(address), admin only. INSTANT: no queue and no timelock. Emits QuoteApproved(quote).
quote.revoke: revokeQuote(address), admin only, instant. Emits QuoteRevoked(quote). Refuses the default quote with DefaultQuoteNotRevocable. Reaches FUTURE launches only: a launched token keeps its quote and its pool forever.
quote.units: startFdvUsdc6, bondFdvUsdc6 and devBuyQuote are raw units of the launch's own quote. The Portal never rescales them, so under an 18-decimal quote they are 18-decimal amounts despite the Usdc6 names.

launching.devBuy: devBuyQuote, in the launch's quote's own units, is pulled from msg.sender with safeTransferFrom inside launch(). Approve the PORTAL for at least devBuyQuote on the quote token first. The pull must deliver exactly devBuyQuote or the launch reverts FeeOnTransferQuote. Whatever the swap does not spend below the 4x price ceiling is refunded in the same transaction. Zero means no dev buy and needs no approval.
launching.oneConfirmation: The Argus site sends the approve and the launch as one EIP-5792 wallet_sendCalls batch where the wallet supports it, and as two transactions where it does not. The launch itself is one transaction either way, so no block has the pool without the dev buy.

payouts.creator: CREDITED, NOT PUSHED. distribute() credits the creator's share to claimableQuote6(creator) on the launch's splitter (index 5 of the record) and emits Accrued(creator, quote, amount). It is delivered by claim(address account): permissionless, anyone may call it, and it always pays account, never the caller. The Argus keeper delivers it; the creator can also claim from the token page.
payouts.treasury: Pushed inside distribute() as Paid(treasury, quote, amount). A failed push parks as PayFailed and is withdrawn with claim(treasury).
payouts.claimable: claimableQuote6(account) and claimableToken18(account) are what claim(account) would pay now, in the quote's own decimals and the token's 18.
payouts.asset: On Portal #6 claim() pays with an ERC-20 transfer of the launch's quote, so it shows as a Transfer log on that token. On Portal #5 it is a native USDC send, which Arc logs from the EIP-7708 pseudo-address 0xffff...fffe.

constants.treasuryAppliesTo: the tax AND the pool's own LP fees; the locker forwards both legs to the same splitter
constants.taxesAreImmutable: There is no reduceTaxes and no owner on this line. Rates are fixed at launch permanently.
constants.taxedEvents: trades only; wallet-to-wallet transfers are untaxed
constants.devBuyMaxBpsNote: 10000 disables the supply cap. What bounds the opening buy is DEV_BUY_MAX_TICK_MOVE.
constants.devBuyPriceCeiling: 4.00x of the opening price; oversized sends are PARTIALLY FILLED AND REFUNDED, not reverted
constants.timelockDelayNote: Pointer changes only. A one-way ratchet: it can be raised to maxTimelockDelaySeconds, never lowered. Quote approval does not wait on it.
